transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Ethan Chen (Polaris Head of Cloud Partnerships), Maya Alvarez (Polaris Security Architect), Tom Reynolds (Polaris Marketplace PM)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, welcome. Quick roll call — Jordan here on the AE side, Priya our SE.
[00:10] Ethan (Polaris): Ethan here, Maya and Tom from Polaris. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:20] Jordan: Awesome. Goal for today is to align on the marketplace listing cadence, reference architecture options, and identify blockers for Polaris to list Redwood in your marketplace. Also want to call out any compliance asks early.
[00:35] Priya (Redwood SE): Yeah hi all, I'll focus on the technical parts — network, auth, recommended deployments, and then we'll propose an initial benchmark plan.
[00:47] Maya (Polaris): Great. From security we mostly care about data residency, KMS, audit logs, and whether we can run in our VPC or need a private deployment.
[00:58] Tom (Polaris): And from marketplace side we want to know SKU options, pricing bands, and the approval timeline.

[01:12] Jordan: Quick question — what's your preferred hosting model for early customers? Are you planning a managed listing or more of a bring-your-own infra?
[01:25] Ethan: For Polaris marketplace we prefer managed listings for quick onboarding, but enterprise buyers often ask for VPC private deployment. So we need both patterns documented.
[01:37] Priya: Okay perfect, that's inline with what Redwood supports — hosted API for self-serve, Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) for predictable throughput, and private deployment options for VPC/on-prem. We'll map both to marketplace SKUs.

[01:55] Maya: On the security front, what's your KMS story? We require customer-managed keys for some enterprise deals.
[02:05] Priya: We integrate with cloud KMS providers and also support customer-managed keys for Private deployments. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption and can provide attestation and key usage logs, but full CMK is only available on Private or Dedicated with KMS integration — I might have garbled that, but essentially CMK is available for private editions or dedicated with a KMS integration.
[02:35] Maya: Ok that makes sense. We'll want an architecture diagram showing where keys live.

[02:48] Tom: Marketplace listing — do you have a suggested SKU breakdown? One-off, pay-as-you-go, reserved?
[02:58] Jordan: Typical approach: pay-as-you-go for hosted (per-token), reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated (monthly/annual), and enterprise licensing for Private. For marketplace we can translate those into listing SKUs — e.g., small/medium/large reserved pools or a payg connector. We'll draft a SKU matrix after this call.

[03:18] Ethan: Great. Also, what's the typical latency profile? A lot of our buyers filter by avg latency.
[03:27] Priya: Depends on model and deployment. Hosted endpoints with smaller models get sub-200ms for short prompts; for larger context windows and bigger models it's higher. We also offer streaming responses and lower-latency variants. We'll include performance profiles in the listing — note though the numbers can vary by region and workload.

[03:50] Jordan: We should explicitly call out fallback behavior in the marketplace description — how Redwood does graceful degradation (model variants, region fallback) so buyers know about reliability.

[04:05] Maya: From compliance — do you provide SOC2 reports and audit logs attached to tenant activity?
[04:14] Priya: Yes we are SOC2 compliant and we can provide audit-log exports; for Private deployments customers can maintain their own retention. For hosted we have tenant-level audit logs with configurable retention (add-on).
[04:30] Maya: Cool. We'll need a copy of SOC2 attestation and sample audit log format.

[04:40] Jordan: Action — we'll upload SOC2 and sample logs to the shared Polaris folder.

[04:48] Tom: Networking question — for Dedicated or Private, will you require VPN or do you support VPC peering/direct connect?
[04:58] Priya: We support VPC peering and direct connect for Private. For Dedicated we can do secure peering as well, but dedicated is in customer-isolated pools within our cloud provider; we can supply a network design. We'll capture recommended NAT/Egress rules and CIDR lists.

[05:18] Ethan: Are there typical egress costs that partners should model? Buyers ask about egress pricing.
[05:26] Priya: Yep, egress and instance GPU costs are the big drivers. We'll provide guidance and an expected cost-per-1000-token table for typical models.

[05:38] Jordan: Let's talk integration steps for marketplace listing — what's Polaris's internal review flow?
[05:45] Tom: We have a product review, security, and legal step. Usually takes 2-3 weeks if all docs are present. Legal often wants a data processing addendum.

[05:55] Jordan: Ok we'll prepare a DPA template and sample contract language for the listing.

[06:05] Maya: On the technical side, we'd like a recommended reference architecture for three scenarios: 1) quick self-serve hosted, 2) Dedicated for mid-market, 3) Private/VPC for enterprise.
[06:20] Priya: We'll prepare diagrams for each: for hosted we'll show standard API w/tenant isolation, for Dedicated we'll show reserved GPU pools with autoscale and customer subnet peering, and for Private we'll show control plane vs data plane separation and on-prem connectors. We'll label the KMS, SSO, and audit log flow.

[06:40] Jordan: Quick note — sometimes our marketing calls Redwood's dedicated product 'Redwood Decide' in transcription, so the word can get munged in automated notes.
[06:50] Ethan: (laughs) we'll watch for that.

[07:00] Priya: On auth — we support OIDC/SAML SSO, RBAC, and token-based API keys. For marketplace we recommend using OIDC integration so Polaris users can SSO into Redwood from within the marketplace. There's an SSO config doc we'll share.

[07:20] Tom: How does billing work for marketplace purchases? Do you have a metering API that we can read for usage-based billing?
[07:28] Jordan: Yes we can expose usage metrics via our billing API and we also push usage events to the marketplace where supported. For reserved contracts we invoice monthly and we can integrate with Polaris' billing pipeline.

[07:45] Maya: A couple security nitty-gritty: can you redact prompts in audit logs, or do you store PII in logs? We have customers who require prompt redaction by default.
[07:55] Priya: We support configurable redaction for logs, and you can choose to not persist full prompts or to mask PII. We'll document the default retention and masking options.

[08:12] Ethan: Good. Let's move to a rough integration timeline — what are the main milestones?
[08:20] Jordan: 1) Docs + listing draft (this week), 2) Security review and SOC2 + network docs (next week), 3) Hands-on workshop + benchmark (week after), 4) Final legal + launch. So 3-5 week window depends on backlog.

[08:40] Tom: For the hands-on, can you run a benchmark using our sample workload? It'll be mostly multi-turn assistant style with context windows up to 4k tokens.
[08:50] Priya: Yes. We'll provision a test queue, run a 10k-token sample set, and report latency and token costs. One ask — please provide 3 representative prompt sets and a traffic profile (QPS, concurrency).

[09:05] Maya: We'll get those by Wednesday. Also, our compliance team needs to meet Priya for 30 minutes to review the reference arch.

[09:15] Priya: Happy to do that — I'll block time.

[09:20] Jordan: Let's capture blockers: any red flags from Polaris?
[09:24] Ethan: Main risk is legal approval cycle; also some enterprise customers want on-prem which may add time.

[09:32] Priya: For on-prem we'll need to scope network and hardware; we can provide an on-prem package but that typically takes longer to approve.

[09:42] Tom: Another question — marketplace product assets. Do you provide marketing collateral and logos in specific formats?
[09:50] Jordan: Yes, we'll provide logos, short/long descriptions, and a 1-pager for the listing. We'll share the assets folder link after this call.

[10:02] Priya: One technical nuance — if you plan to enable autoscaling with burst capacity, we recommend setting a warm pool for critical workloads to meet latency SLOs. We'll include recommended scaling policies in the reference arch doc.

[10:20] Ethan: Any competitor concerns we should address in the listing copy? Customers ask why choose Redwood vs GCP/AWS vendor-managed offerings.

[10:30] Jordan: Highlight production-first experience, predictable economics, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, and strong observability. We'll craft a short competitive differentiator line for the marketplace.

[10:45] Maya: Can we have a demo of the audit log export and SSO flow? Might be helpful for security review.

[10:52] Priya: Yes — we'll capture a short video and screenshots, and include steps to configure SAML/SCIM.

[11:05] Tom: For the launch checklist, can we agree on items Polaris needs from Redwood vs what Redwood needs from Polaris?

[11:13] Jordan: Sure — Redwood provides listing draft, SOC2, SKUs, asset pack, reference architecture, benchmark results. Polaris provides network diagram, review contacts (security/legal), and approval timeline.

[11:30] Ethan: Sounds good. Any other open technical questions?

[11:34] Maya: One more — how are model updates handled for a listed product? If you change model versions, do customers get notified or is it a rollout?

[11:44] Priya: We support model version pinning per customer and rollouts (canary, A/B). We can document policy for updates and notification practices. We'll include the rollout policy in the technical appendix.

[11:58] Jordan: Ok, recap and next steps — Jordan to send listing draft and assets link by 2026-05-28; Priya to send reference architecture and schedule compliance review by 2026-05-27; Polaris (Maya/Tom) to provide network diagram and legal reviewer by 2026-05-26; schedule workshop week of 2026-06-01.

[12:20] Ethan: Thanks all — this is helpful. We'll aim to get materials early next week.

[12:30] Tom: Thanks, talk soon.

[12:35] Jordan: Thanks everyone, closing the call.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "Dedicated" -> "Decided"), speaker labels auto-generated; timestamps approximate.
